memory_update.text: AJINY should be tracked as the most direct US-accessible public mapping to ABF insulating film, but the semiconductor exposure is embedded inside a broader food/bioscience conglomerate.

MECG.F / 4971.T is a high-priority underfollowed chemistry candidate for copper-to-resin adhesion in package substrates; later layers must verify revenue purity, customer concentration, and market-share durability.
IBIDY is a reference substrate leader rather than the ideal underfollowed small/mid-cap target because its market cap and specialist awareness exceed the preferred hunting range.
AMKR is not a substrate or ABF supplier; keep it in the universe only as a direct advanced-packaging platform/customer read-through for substrate and HBM package demand.

Several highly relevant substrate makers, including Unimicron, Kinsus, AT&S, and Shinko, may be better direct fits but require separate verification of US tradability, ADR/OTC ticker quality, liquidity, and current corporate status before inclusion in a US-listed universe.

No clean US-listed pure-play equivalent was identified for the highest-scarcity materials named in the provided evidence: Ajinomoto build-up film and MEC copper-adhesion surface chemistry. Treat US-listed names as adjacent proxies unless direct supplier/customer evidence emerges.
AMKR is a second-order advanced-packaging capacity proxy for the FC-BGA/AI accelerator package node, but evidence must separate AI/HPC advanced-packaging exposure from broader OSAT cyclicality.
ONTO is a plausible underfollowed yield-control proxy because it explicitly targets advanced IC substrates, panel-level packaging, and AI/HPC applications with inspection/metrology tools.

CAMT is a plausible mid-cap advanced-packaging inspection/metrology proxy with explicit HBM and heterogeneous-integration order evidence, but customer concentration and order cyclicality require verification.

For US-listed equities, the node maps better to advanced-packaging yield-control tools and capacity infrastructure than to direct ownership of the scarce insulating film or copper surface-chemistry suppliers.

MKSI should be tracked as the strongest US-listed substrate-chemistry/process-equipment proxy via Atotech, but purity must be verified because MKS is diversified across broader semiconductor and industrial process technologies.
CAMT has direct HBM/OSAT order evidence and fits the preferred mid-cap underfollowed lane for advanced-packaging inspection/metrology.
ONTO is a larger but relevant US-listed inspection/metrology and analytics proxy for advanced IC substrates, panel-level packaging, and AI/HPC package yield control.

The purest substrate makers and chemistry bottleneck names cited in the source material, including Ibiden, Unimicron, Kinsus, AT&S, Shinko, Ajinomoto, and MEC Company, are not clean US-primary-listed small/mid-cap candidates; later passes should decide whether OTC ADRs/foreign listings are allowed.

For US-listed names, the investable Layer 1B mapping is more indirect: process chemistry/equipment, inspection/metrology, OSAT/advanced packaging, and test gates rather than pure FC-BGA substrate manufacturing.

MKSI should be tracked as the strongest US-listed underfollowed proxy for advanced packaging wet chemistry, plating, package-substrate surface treatment, and copper/RDL process exposure through Atotech.
FORM should be tracked as an HBM and advanced-package yield-control candidate through probe cards and known-good-die testing, not as a substrate maker.

ONTO should be tracked as an inspection/metrology beneficiary of AI-package complexity, especially where panel substrates, 3D bump metrology, RDL, and macro defect inspection become yield bottlenecks.

US-listed direct pure-play exposure to FC-BGA substrates, ABF insulating film, and copper adhesion chemistry appears limited; many core substrate and materials names are Japan/Taiwan-listed, so US-listed exposure is mostly adjacent through chemistry, test, inspection, and OSAT capacity.

Layer 2 should verify whether any US-listed ADRs or OTC securities for Japan/Taiwan substrate and chemistry leaders are investable enough for inclusion, while keeping this Layer 1B list focused on primary US exchange-listed names.
